chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Fazzal, from Dawood ibn Abu Yazeed al-Attar, from one of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).

Regarding a man who had a wife, a man came with witnesses that this woman is the wife of so-and-so, and others came and testified that she is the wife of so-and-so. The witnesses were all just and deemed reliable. He (peace be upon him) said: A lot is drawn between the witnesses; whoever's lot comes out, he is the rightful one, and he is the first to have the right to her.

key_terms.أَوْلَى بِهَا: First to have the right to her

ai.seo_question: How is a woman's marital status determined when two equally reliable witnesses claim she is their wife?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Kafi illustrates the Shia juristic principle of 'qara'' (drawing lots) to resolve conflicting claims of equal evidentiary weight, reflecting the pragmatic approach to uncertainty in marital disputes. It highlights the Imam's role in establishing procedural justice when witness testimony is balanced, ensuring social order through a divinely sanctioned method of resolution.
